logs.summary: Torrential rain starting late on August 13, 2023, caused record-breaking flooding in eastern Japan, particularly in Chiba Prefecture. The flooding resulted in at least eight to nine deaths, widespread power outages affecting over 22,000 households, and stranded thousands of travelers at Tokyo's Narita Airport. Authorities issued the highest-level rain warnings as the region experienced unprecedented rainfall, equivalent to three months' worth in 12 hours.

logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

news.headline: Médecins Sans Frontières Launches 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition to Spotlight Humanitarian Crises and Ebola Disease Outbreak in DRC
news.body: HONG KONG, July 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) Hong Kong yesterday held an opening ceremony for its 'Keep Life Breathing' Roving Exhibition. As a key part of its annual 'MSF Day' campaign, the exhibition will tour three locations throughout July: The Wai, Festival Walk, and TKO Plaza. It showcases real-life stories of MSF providing emergency medical humanitarian assistance to people affected by protracted conflicts and crises. The event also features an Ebola disease-themed zone, which aims to deepen public awareness and understanding of the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

incidents.summary:
Severe drought expanded into southeast North Dakota, with Fargo nearly 8 inches below normal rainfall. Oklahoma City recorded one of its hottest, driest Augusts on record. France announced hundreds of millions in drought aid for affected farmers, and Oxfam warned of a growing food crisis in Central America’s Dry Corridor due to El Niño-driven crop losses. A drone project in Alaska demonstrated successful cloud seeding to combat drought, while Comanche County extended burn bans amid extreme wildfire risk.
New reports show drought widening impacts: the Ross Fire in Texas grew to 90,000 acres amid extreme heat, over 60% of Canadians reported personal climate disaster effects, Kenya's food import bill rose 21% due to crop failure, and Puerto Rico marked 10 years of oversight under a severe water crisis. Additionally, South Africa, Zambia, and Jamaica faced heightened El Niño risks, while Colorado farmers suffered mental health tolls from prolonged drought.

Other reports highlighted severe drought in Wisconsin, reduced grain harvests in Germany, and the potential for a super El Niño affecting Latin America and Sri Lanka.

logs.summary:
Severe drought expanded into southeast North Dakota, with Fargo nearly 8 inches below normal rainfall. Oklahoma City recorded one of its hottest, driest Augusts on record. France announced hundreds of millions in drought aid for affected farmers, and Oxfam warned of a growing food crisis in Central America’s Dry Corridor due to El Niño-driven crop losses. A drone project in Alaska demonstrated successful cloud seeding to combat drought, while Comanche County extended burn bans amid extreme wildfire risk.
New reports show drought widening impacts: the Ross Fire in Texas grew to 90,000 acres amid extreme heat, over 60% of Canadians reported personal climate disaster effects, Kenya's food import bill rose 21% due to crop failure, and Puerto Rico marked 10 years of oversight under a severe water crisis. Additionally, South Africa, Zambia, and Jamaica faced heightened El Niño risks, while Colorado farmers suffered mental health tolls from prolonged drought.

news.headline: Amid Severe Water Crisis & Drought, Puerto Rico Marks 10 Years of “La Junta” Oversight
news.body: Juan Carlos Dávila reports from Puerto Rico as the island grapples with a severe water crisis. A record-breaking drought has led to severe shortages and a system of water rationing that residents say could have been prevented by better infrastructure maintenance. Climate scientists have warned for years that changing weather conditions in the Caribbean are likely to exacerbate existing infrastructure failings, but rather than address the root cause of the water shortage, explains Dávila, a pattern of government inaction and failed public services is used to justify increasing privatization. Puerto Rico’s water woes come 10 years after the United States passed the bankruptcy law PROMESA to restructure the U.S. territory’s debt, installing an unelected board colloquially known as “La Junta” that continues to hold sweeping authority to determine fiscal and public policy. “This water crisis taking place right now in Puerto Rico, also La Junta bears some responsibility on it,” says Puerto Rican investigative reporter Luis Valentín. “It did not reduce the debt, and [so] pretty much crowds out resources that could be used for infrastructure work.”

The death toll from Russia's deadliest strike on Ukraine this year, targeting a warehouse west of Kyiv, has risen to 38, with four people still missing, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
On August 31, India's PM Modi met Putin at the SCO summit in Bishkek, urging a peaceful resolution to the war in Ukraine. Russia's Defense Ministry announced preparations for "massive strikes" on Ukraine's energy infrastructure following its deadliest attack of the year. Ukraine is racing to develop new interceptors to counter Russian drones and missiles, while a Russian drone attack hit an ammunition depot near Kyiv. Additionally, 22 Filipino seafarers were safely repatriated after their ship was attacked in the Black Sea.

Meanwhile, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russia's Lavrov in Manila, expressing readiness to help end the war but noting no quick deal is imminent.
Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Wildberries warehouses produced massive pillars of black smoke as fires raged at the facilities. Russia, stretched by Ukraine's drone attacks on its Black Sea Fleet, has pulled all warships from the Mediterranean Sea. Both sides have increased bridge strikes to disrupt resupply networks, indicating expectations of a prolonged stalemate, while the Kremlin warned against optimism on peace following the Rubio-Lavrov meeting.
The EU passed its 21st sanctions package with 218 new designations targeting Russia, including vessels that refuel shadow fleet tankers. Ukrainian strikes continued to hit Russian Wildberries warehouses, while new airstrikes caused deaths in both Ukraine and Russia, and a drone was shot down over NATO airspace.

CIA Director Ratcliffe's secret Moscow visit reportedly included a proposal for a trilateral Trump-Putin-Zelensky meeting, while Russia resumed strikes on Kyiv following a deadly attack on a care home that killed 34. Addressing the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, he advocated for a peaceful resolution, stating that India is the land of Mahatma Gandhi and Gautam Buddha and stands firmly for peace while supporting efforts to end the war. He noted that every step taken towards ending the war energises peace, whereas actions prolonging it act against humanity. news.headline: PM meets Vladimir Putin at SCO sidelines in Bishkek, calls for end to Ukraine war
news.body: This news report covers key geopolitical, economic, and strategic developments involving India, Russia, West Asia, and North America. During a bilateral meeting at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Russian President Vladimir Putin that the world must transition from endless wars to an end of war regarding the Russia-Ukraine conflict, emphasizing peace and dialogue. Both leaders discussed bilateral ties, trade, and defence cooperation while travelling together to the Nomad Games opening ceremony. Additionally, the broadcast analyzes India's strategic partnership with Russia ahead of the SCO and BRICS summits, focusing on Arctic shipping routes, trade imbalances, and currency mechanisms. The report also highlights India's first-quarter GDP growth of 7.8 percent, driven by domestic consumption and exports. Further coverage includes escalating West Asia tensions following United States military airstrikes on Iranian installations on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz, alongside PM Modi's diplomatic engagement with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Finally, it details Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh Sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat's global outreach tour across the United States and Canada.

incidents.summary:
On August 30-31, U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iran to retaliate with ballistic missiles on U.S. bases in Jordan and a drone intercepted by the UAE. President Trump described Iran as a "failed nation" and threatened further strikes, but ruled out nuclear weapons, while oil prices rose over 2.5% on supply disruption fears. Trump’s approval fell to a new low of 32% per a UMass poll, and he plans to meet with U.S. refiners to address high fuel prices.
On September 1, the US launched large-scale strikes on Iranian Revolutionary Guards targets, its first direct mainland attacks in over a month, prompting Iran to retaliate with drones and missiles and vow "severe punishment." Oil prices surged over 4% as hostilities reignited after a fragile lull, while Iran urged the US to honor an interim agreement. Separately, Treasury Secretary Bessent stated at the G20 that US allies support the economic war against Iran, and Europe faces a winter energy crunch from the conflict.

logs.summary:
The U.S. and Iran have paused attacks and resumed diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, with mediators reporting progress and talks focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, the Pentagon quietly removed four recent troop deaths from its official Iran war death toll, reclassifying them in a new category, sparking controversy. Additional concerns include the U.S.'s dangerously low weaponry supply and growing public skepticism over the war’s costs and duration.
Mediators reported that neither the U.S. nor Iran conducted any attacks for three consecutive days, signaling progress in ceasefire efforts. New polls indicate that only one in three Americans now support the war, the lowest reading since the conflict began, and a majority view it as going "very badly." The Pentagon continued to face scrutiny over its reclassification of four troop deaths from the conflict.

logs.summary:
US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on August 30, the first direct military action in weeks, prompting Iran to retaliate with ballistic missile attacks on US bases in Jordan. President Trump claimed that Iran's Kharg Island was "blown to smithereens," though no confirmation was provided. The exchange marks a significant escalation after a period of diplomatic and economic pressure.
On August 31, Trump called Iran a "failed nation" and posted an AI-generated video falsely claiming Kharg Island was destroyed. Iran retaliated further by firing a drone at the UAE, and oil prices surged above $90/barrel amid renewed hostilities.

logs.summary:
On August 30-31, U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iran to retaliate with ballistic missiles on U.S. bases in Jordan and a drone intercepted by the UAE. President Trump described Iran as a "failed nation" and threatened further strikes, but ruled out nuclear weapons, while oil prices rose over 2.5% on supply disruption fears. Trump’s approval fell to a new low of 32% per a UMass poll, and he plans to meet with U.S. refiners to address high fuel prices.
On September 1, the US launched large-scale strikes on Iranian Revolutionary Guards targets, its first direct mainland attacks in over a month, prompting Iran to retaliate with drones and missiles and vow "severe punishment." Oil prices surged over 4% as hostilities reignited after a fragile lull, while Iran urged the US to honor an interim agreement. Separately, Treasury Secretary Bessent stated at the G20 that US allies support the economic war against Iran, and Europe faces a winter energy crunch from the conflict.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

news.headline: Wildfires Rage in Greece as Heat Wave Grips Europe
news.body: In Greece, two firefighters were killed Sunday when two helicopters battling a massive wildfire collided west of Athens. Two other crew members in one of the helicopters were rescued. More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight this weekend in blazes that broke out around the coastal village of Porto Germeno. Hundreds of people have been evacuated. This is a local resident. Giorgos Mavroidis: “It’s not a good situation. This is extremely sad. The wind is very strong and keeps changing direction. It’s difficult to deal with. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

The United Kingdom recorded its driest July in nearly two centuries. Strong winds returned in Greece, pushing flames into mountain home clusters, destroying farms and property, and closing a highway. In France, firefighters guarded against flare-ups near Bordeaux. The U.K. weather service reported a prolonged heat wave and lack of rainfall. Europe is the fastest-warming continent, with rising temperatures and droughts making wildfires more intense.

news.headline: Europe Battles Extreme Weather: France, Spain, Serbia & Bosnia Hit By Wildfires, Floods And Storms
news.body: Extreme weather is gripping multiple European nations as severe wildfires, flash floods and powerful storms force thousands of people to evacuate. France is battling a major wildfire across the Cap Ferret Peninsula in the southwest, where extreme summer heat and months of drought have created dangerous fire conditions. Authorities ordered the evacuation of the popular tourism hotspot as flames threatened homes and the peninsula’s main escape route. More than 10,000 hectares of forest have reportedly been affected, while around 63,000 people, including large numbers of tourists, were forced to leave the area. Boats and emergency teams were deployed as authorities worked to protect residents and visitors. Spain is also facing a contrasting weather crisis, with intense wildfires occurring alongside torrential rainfall and flash flooding. Heavy rains disrupted road and rail transport and injured more than 11 people.

In response, British Columbia declared a state of emergency as crews faced challenging conditions from severe drought and windy weather.

Two new developments emerged 19 days after the earthquake: Latin artists Juanes and Alejandro Sanz launched "Marea Viva" to support rebuilding efforts in the hard-hit Chocó region. Meanwhile, families have launched a desperate, citizen-led search for hundreds of pets that fled or went missing in the rubble.
Two weeks after the earthquake, a municipal survey in Cali found around 25,000 people lacking adequate housing, with 10,000 families affected and many sheltering with relatives or searching in a strained rental market. Criticism continued over President De La Espriella's response, with an article describing his actions as tawdry and focused on far-right allies.

Additional severe weather warnings and storm threats affected regions from the Plains to the Northeast, including Duke Energy outages in Charlotte, North Carolina.
Ongoing power outages continue in San Antonio, Texas, with over 26,000 residents still without electricity days after severe storms, and CPS Energy providing updates. Scattered storms and localized flooding threats are expected across Northeast Florida and Southeast Georgia, while spotty storms are reported in central and northeastern KELOLAND (South Dakota).

Confirmed tornadoes struck in Atlantic Beach (Long Island), Dover (Delaware), and York/Lancaster counties (Pennsylvania), while prolonged power outages from earlier storms left thousands without electricity in Gary, Indiana, for over a week. Widespread damage from downed trees, damaged homes, and flooding was reported in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Southeast, and Midwest.

logs.summary:
New tornadoes confirmed in New York: an EF-1 and EF-0 near Wilton, and two tornadoes (EF-0 and EF-1) touched down in the state on Thursday, with damage surveys ongoing. Severe thunderstorms caused widespread power outages in San Antonio, Texas, leaving up to 100,000 customers without power and thousands potentially facing days without electricity amid heat index values above 100. Additional severe weather warnings and storm threats affected regions from the Plains to the Northeast, including Duke Energy outages in Charlotte, North Carolina.
Ongoing power outages continue in San Antonio, Texas, with over 26,000 residents still without electricity days after severe storms, and CPS Energy providing updates. Scattered storms and localized flooding threats are expected across Northeast Florida and Southeast Georgia, while spotty storms are reported in central and northeastern KELOLAND (South Dakota).

logs.summary:
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region near Ende on August 14, 2026, toppling buildings and killing at least two people. The shallow quake triggered a tsunami warning for four provinces, prompting mass evacuations before the alert was later lifted. Several strong aftershocks were reported.
The death toll from the magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Ende, Indonesia has risen to at least 38, with dozens injured and many buildings collapsed or damaged. Rescuers are searching for survivors in affected areas, and tsunami waves of less than 1 meter were recorded in several locations before the warning was lifted.

news.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia, tsunami warning issued - West Hawaii Today
news.body: JAKARTA (Reuters) — An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and several aftershocks struck off the coast of eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the nation’s geophysics agency BMKG said, while tsunami waves of less than 1 metre (3 feet) were recorded in several areas. Many rushed from their homes, but there were no initial reports of damage from the quake, which was felt strongly for around one minute in regions such as Nagekeo and Bima, said Dodi Yuleova, the spokesperson for the national disaster mitigation agency. A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as located at a port in Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed parts of a building collapsing in dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street. A hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed. BMKG recorded the first quake at 4:58 a.m. (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by several aftershocks.

logs.summary:
The recovery from the M7.7 earthquake continues as Indonesia's Public Works Minister vows to rebuild damaged public facilities in East Nusa Tenggara. Caritas Indonesia is actively assisting in affected areas, and the Health Ministry has deployed 206 medical reserve volunteers to restore healthcare services in the region.
As of late August, the number of earthquake evacuees in East Nusa Tenggara is declining as aftershocks begin to ease. Recovery efforts are shifting focus to long-term rebuilding, with special attention to the needs of affected children, while tourism authorities in Labuan Bajo assess post-quake recovery for the region's tourism industry.

logs.summary: A large wildfire ignited in the High Fens nature reserve in eastern Belgium (Liège province) around August 14, 2026, destroying approximately 3,000 hectares (12 square miles) of land. Firefighters from Belgium, Germany, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands battled the blaze, which threatened to spread into Germany and prompted partial evacuations in the border town of Monschau. Rain on August 17 brought some relief, slowing the fire's advance towards the German border.

incidents.summary:
The death toll from the Bagmati floods has risen above 1,000 across Nepal and China, with rescue teams continuing efforts to reach hundreds feared trapped in hydropower tunnels. A headteacher evacuated 900 students just minutes before floodwaters swept away their school, a widely reported story. Meanwhile, fresh flood alerts have been issued as water levels rise, and the US State Department has warned against travel to affected areas, while survivors express fears of losing their culture and communities.
Rescue teams have reached previously inaccessible remote areas, with the number of missing in Nepal reported at 3,916 including 80 Americans. The disaster caused an estimated $5 billion in damages, raising concerns about Nepal's hydropower ambitions, and a UN official warned of severe glacial flood risks ahead. Personal stories continue to emerge, including the search for missing Chinese workers and a family's desperate four-day search for a lost son.

logs.summary: A glacier collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border triggered devastating flash floods and mudslides on August 26, 2026, sweeping through several communities in the Bagmati region. The disaster has killed hundreds of people (with death tolls reported between 350 and 500) and left over 1,300 missing, including dozens of foreign nationals. Rescue teams are searching for survivors while authorities warn of additional flood risks from a newly formed lake, and international aid is arriving to support relief efforts.

news.headline: Aug. 27: Flash Flooding Overwhelms Nepal, and Jury Deliberates in Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Trial
news.body: Devastating flash floods and mudslides wreaked havoc along the Nepal-China border this week, leaving hundreds dead and more than 1,000 missing. More than 500 foreigners are among the missing, including, by one estimate, roughly 65 Americans. NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer explains why the destruction happened without warning and what role climate change may have played. Then, jury deliberations are underway in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who killed her three young children. While Clancy doesn’t dispute the killings, her defense team is arguing that she shouldn’t be held criminally responsible because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. But the prosecution insists she acted intentionally and deliberately. As the jury weighs a set of complex outcomes, NBC News legal analyst Misty Marris breaks down what evidence and testimony from the five-week trial could be key to reaching a verdict. Finally, 2026 could be the year of the foldable phone. Samsung and Google already have models on the market, and Apple is reportedly planning to drop its version in September. But are consumers willing to shell out $2,000 for a little extra screen? NBC News chief tech analyst Joanna Stern explains why the phones have appeal.

As of August 31, the death toll from the Bagmati flash floods has surpassed 950 (with 955 confirmed and over 900 in Nepal alone), while the number of missing has climbed to nearly 5,000, including dozens of Americans and other foreign nationals. Rescue efforts are focused on freeing hundreds of workers trapped in hydropower tunnels, with foreign specialists from India, China, and South Korea assisting. New flood warnings remain in effect as water levels rise, and China faces accusations of concealing the disaster's scale in Tibet, while stories of heroism (e.g., a principal evacuating 900 students) and ongoing humanitarian challenges emerge.

news.headline: “Catastrophe of Unimaginable Proportions”: Nepal Flood Death Toll Tops 900; Near 5,000 Still Missing
news.body: More than 900 people in Nepal are confirmed dead after a massive wall of water, mud and debris crashed through a Himalayan river valley on the border with Tibet. More than 4,200 people are missing in Nepal and hundreds more in Tibet. Families are searching hospitals for loved ones, and crews have buried hundreds of unidentified bodies in shallow graves. Rescue efforts are also underway for more than 900 hydropower workers, believed to be trapped in more than a dozen underground tunnels blocked by debris. The cause of the flash flooding is believed to have been the collapse of a glacier in the mountains, leading a wave of water, rocks and debris to carve its way through the valley. “This is a catastrophe of unimaginable proportions,” says journalist Kunda Dixit, speaking to Democracy Now! from the Nepalese capital of Kathmandu. “We used to say that the glaciers are melting in the Himalaya. Now it seems like the mountains are cracking up,” says Dixit. “This has sort of redefined what global warming and climate change is doing, not just to Nepal and the Himalaya, but to the planet.”

logs.summary:
The death toll from the Bagmati floods has risen above 1,000 across Nepal and China, with rescue teams continuing efforts to reach hundreds feared trapped in hydropower tunnels. A headteacher evacuated 900 students just minutes before floodwaters swept away their school, a widely reported story. Meanwhile, fresh flood alerts have been issued as water levels rise, and the US State Department has warned against travel to affected areas, while survivors express fears of losing their culture and communities.
Rescue teams have reached previously inaccessible remote areas, with the number of missing in Nepal reported at 3,916 including 80 Americans. The disaster caused an estimated $5 billion in damages, raising concerns about Nepal's hydropower ambitions, and a UN official warned of severe glacial flood risks ahead. Personal stories continue to emerge, including the search for missing Chinese workers and a family's desperate four-day search for a lost son.
